---
title: "How to Create Stand-Alone Monthly Invoices"
---

## **Purpose & Background**

This SOP describes how AR creates monthly subscription invoices as stand-alone invoices in Rillet.

The original SOP, _How to Create Monthly Subscription Invoices_, used Rillet's usage-upload method. That process is currently on hold because of a Rillet limitation:

- Rillet still allows invoice creation through usage upload (fill out a template, upload it, invoices are generated).
- However, the invoice date and revenue-recognition month produced by usage upload do not match how Latchel processes invoices.

Workaround: Until Rillet resolves this, Latchel creates a stand-alone invoice for each customer. This is the only method that lets AR choose the preferred invoice date and recognize revenue in the correct month.

Many of the preparation steps mirror the original usage-upload SOP, in particular, preparing the billing count sources described in the next section.

## Prepare the Billing Count Sources

Before creating any invoices, prepare and pre-fill the billing count sources. As in the original SOP, review each source and confirm it is complete and ready.

Billing counts come from three sources:

1. Billing Input Module (BIM) — completed by the CPT team, usually around the 6th day of the month.
2. By portfolio - custom instructions for each included customer is described  
3. Unit Count Data Sheet - automatically pulled every last day of the previous month  

Because the BIM depends on CPT completion, sequence the work so BIM-based invoices are created last. Start with portfolio-billed customers, then unit-count customers, then BIM customers.

Having these sources pre-filled and ready before the actual invoice run makes the process far more seamless.

## **Step 1: Build the Monthly Invoice Creation Tracker**

Invoices can be created directly from each customer's Rillet profile, but AR keeps a tracker first for organization. A pre-filled tracker makes the creation run smoother and gives an early view of the total number of invoices for the month.

1. Set up the sheet
   1. Create a new _(Month)_ Invoice Creation Tracker sheet.
   2. Open the CC fee/autopay tracker and copy the customer name and CC fee columns into the new sheet.
   3. Filter the CC fee column and delete terminated accounts. What remains is the list of active customers that need invoices, and your total invoice count for the month.
2. Separate CC-fee tabs (recommended practice) - Duplicate the tab, rename it by whether the CC fee is Yes or No, and keep the same columns; only the CC fee application differs between the two tabs.
   1. Split the list into two tabs: 
      1.  Customers with a credit card processing fee 
      2. Customers without a credit card processing fee  

**Column Guide**

![](data:image/png;base64,)

> **_Note: Columns A–D should be pre-filled before invoice creation begins. Columns E–H are filled during creation and used later for the Bridge Report._**

> **_Reminder: For a new customer's first invoice or after a contract update, build the invoice from the actual contract to ensure rates and subscription line items are accurate._**

## **Step 2: Create the Stand-Alone Invoices in Rillet**

Open the customer's invoice screen

1. Go to the customer's Rillet profile and click the Invoice tab.
2. Open last month's invoice in a new tab as a reference, and click Add invoice in the current tab.

Fill out the invoice fields

1. Invoice date: the 1st of the current month (default for all customers).
2. Due date: based on the customer's net term — from their contract or column D of the tracker.
3. Rillet invoicing account: _Analyzed Checking_ (default).
4. Under the Products tab, click Add product to show the full list of Latchel products.
5. Check each product the customer subscribes to, referencing the most current contract or last month's invoice for product names and pricing.
6. Click Add.
7. Fill in the rate and quantity for each product per what the customer has.
8. Record last month's and the current month's net revenue in tracker columns E and F, and fill in the remaining columns.
9. Click Save.

Repeat for every customer on the list.

Here’s a Loom video recording of how standalone invoices are created: [<u>https://www.loom.com/share/b0b80d703f6c48abb5d6b5b4059f8f4e</u>](https://www.loom.com/share/b0b80d703f6c48abb5d6b5b4059f8f4e)

## **Step 3: Handle Special Cases**

**Customers with a monthly minimum**

1. Some customers have a minimum commitment. If a customer's invoice revenue falls below their minimum, add the Latchel Services product with a rate that brings the total up to the minimum.

- _Example:_ revenue reaches \$192, and the minimum is \$200 → add a Latchel Services line at a \$8 rate to close the gap.

2. Customers with a minimum commitment also have a future-dated invoice for the month equal to their minimum. Because you are creating the invoice manually, apply a credit memo to zero out that future-dated invoice. This ensures only one correct invoice — with the right usage and rates — is sent to the customer. (Follow the credit memo guide for the steps.)

**Customers with credits, overpayments, or adjustments**

Because invoices are created manually, check the month's list of customers with credits and apply them. When adding products, add the appropriate adjustment product:

- Credit — for goodwill, active-unit adjustments, and similar.
- Overpayment — for an overpayment carried from a previous month's payment.

If a credit card processing fee applies, also deduct the credit/overpayment amount from the CC fee quantity.

## **Step 4: Raise Count Discrepancies and Follow Up**

As you work, you will encounter sudden increases or decreases in unit count. Flag these before creating the invoice, especially when the change is large.

- Create an Accounts Receivable post tagging both the CSM and the Data team.
- This confirms the correct count before invoicing and helps avoid disputes after invoices go out.

Rule of thumb: It is always better to send an invoice after the 10th than to send an incorrect one. The final say on unit count comes from the CSM and is approved by the FM — and it must be documented in the thread/post.

## **Step 5: Add Late Fees**

Some customers have late fees applicable. Current practice:

- Apply late fees to customers with an invoice unpaid for over 30 days. Make sure that Late fee application is based on what is applicable in their contract.  This can be 1.5% of their over-30-day balance or a flat rate of \$100.  (This is discussed during Monthly AR Aging Sync; make sure the application is approved by FM) 
- Apply late fees consistently to Intrepid Professional Group and Valenti Real Estate depending on their open balance. Use the dedicated late-fee tracker to identify 1.5% of all open invoices for these two accounts.

## **Step 6: Bridge the Draft Invoices Against the Prior Month**

The Bridge Report is a required part of the process. It surfaces unusual changes or discrepancies in billing before invoices are finalized.

1. Generate the Bridge Report.
2. Compare the draft invoice amounts against the previous month.
3. Address any discrepancies before invoices are sent.

Tracker columns E–H (last month's revenue, current revenue, difference, and reason) feed directly into this step. Follow the Bridge Report guide to complete it accurately. Here’s a designated SOP for a step-by-step guide on how to create the Bridge Report

## **Step 7: Send Invoices to Customers (10th of the Month)**

On the 10th day of the month, send the invoices through Rillet.

1. Navigate to Accounts Receivable → Invoices.
2. Set the filter to the criteria below and click Apply:
   - Status: Unbilled
   - Invoice date: dates of the current invoice month
   - Check Only show unsent invoices
3. _(Recommended)_ Click the Customer Name header to sort alphabetically. This makes it easier to spot issues, such as a PM with multiple invoices in error.
4. Click the three dots to the far right of the first unbilled invoice, then click Send.
5. Click Yes, then confirm.
6. Repeat until every unbilled invoice in the list is sent.

## **Step 8: Post-Send Checks**

After all invoices are sent:

1. Post in the #accounts-receivable Slack channel confirming that all invoices have been sent.
2. Check the billing@ email for undelivered invoices, and record them in the Billing@ Undelivered Invoices tracker.
